source.title: MEDITRON-70B: Scaling Medical Pretraining for Large Language Models
source.authors: Zeming Chen; Alejandro Hern'andez Cano; Angelika Romanou; Antoine Bonnet; Kyle Matoba; Francesco Salvi; Matteo Pagliardini; Si-Min Fan; Andreas Kopf; Amirkeivan Mohtashami; Alexandre Sallinen; Alireza Sakhaeirad; Vinitra Swamy; Igor Krawczuk; Deniz Bayazit; Axel Marmet; Syrielle Montariol; Mary-Anne Hartley; Martin Jaggi; Antoine Bosselut

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation language-model loss during continued pretraining as tokens are processed, but does not perform the multi-run scaling-law fits or extrapolation needed to test the claimed power-law relationship.
record.gate_note: Figure 4 reports training and validation loss over processed tokens, and the text says both decrease. This is relevant to the loss-versus-tokens part of V1, but the study does not fit or assess a power law. Downstream benchmark evaluations are not used to fit or test a prediction from scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study builds and evaluates medical LLMs (MEDITRON 7B/70B) by continued pretraining of Llama-2. It cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. only in the introduction. It runs no size, data or compute sweep and fits no power law, and nothing in it tests or extrapolates a scaling law. The one loss figure (Fig. 4) is a single run's training curve, whose shape also depends on the cosine learning-rate schedule. That says nothing about loss scaling across parameters, tokens or compute when the other two are not the bottleneck.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct but narrow. The paper's main conclusion is that continued pretraining of Llama-2 on curated medical data (GAP-Replay) yields MEDITRON models that beat open baselines at matched scale and come within about 10% of larger commercial models. The loss curve is reported only to show learning without overfitting. No scaling-law conclusion is drawn.
record.recipe_differences: A single 70B model is continued-pretrained on medical-domain data; the study does not run a model/data/compute scaling sweep or fit scaling laws.

fits_no_version.finding: During a single 70B continued-pretraining run, validation LM loss falls as tokens are processed, and the authors say there is no overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-run validation loss decreases during domain-adaptive continued pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: Average 5-shot medical-benchmark accuracy across checkpoints of one run rises from 60.8 (0B tokens) to 61.2, 61.4, 61.5 and 63.3 (48B tokens). Individual benchmarks fluctuate and some dip below the base model (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy improves non-monotonically over continued-pretraining checkpoints.

fits_no_version.finding: Of three peak learning rates in 7B GAP-Replay runs, the highest (3e-4) gives the lowest validation loss curve (Fig. 5, appendix D.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The learning rate during continued pretraining affects domain validation loss.

record.problems: The relevant loss trend is shown only in a plot, without reported numerical values or uncertainty. Only one 70B continued-pretraining run is shown for this loss analysis, and no power-law fit is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Training loss is also plotted in Figure 4, but it is not held-out loss, the behavior named by V1.

untested.parts: All of it: there is no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute, and no multi-run sweep.
All of it: the continued-pretraining and fine-tuning runs fit no scaling law.
All of it: the 7B vs 70B and checkpoint accuracy comparisons are not fitted or predicted from scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 is wrong: a single training curve with no fit does not test V1. The 7B vs 70B accuracy gaps and the per-checkpoint accuracies could be mistaken for V6 evidence. They are two sizes and one run's checkpoints, with no predictive fit, so they are not V6 tests.

versions.untested_parts: Whether loss follows a power law; parameter-count and compute scaling; multiple model sizes or runs; several-orders-of-magnitude scaling.

rows.subject: M EDI T RON -70B
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation language-model loss during continued pretraining.

conditions.value: curve plotted across processed tokens; axis extends to 50 billion

rows.note: The text states that validation loss decreases as the model consumes more tokens, but reports no power-law fit or quantitative loss values.
rows.check: This is one 70B continued-pretraining run's validation loss plotted against processed tokens (about 1.34 to 1.24 read off Fig. 4, no reported numbers). A within-run learning curve under a cosine LR schedule is not a scaling-law measurement across models or token budgets. No power law is fitted, so it cannot bear on V1. It also starts from an already-pretrained Llama-2, so it is not pretraining loss from scratch.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
